newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK blue chips end sharply higher, H-shares slide.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips end sharply higher, H-shares slide.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chips ended with solid gains on Monday after gathering momentum during the afternoon following some heavy losses last week, but H-shares ended the day depressed as Chinese stock markets nosedived.
The Hang Seng index ended 153.41 points higher at 12,937.48 after dropping 318.66 points last week. Turnover was HK$6.54 billion, down from Friday's HK$10.10 billion.

"The market has tested the support level so local shares are just bouncing back," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities. "If you look at the fundamental factors they remain quite solid."

James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said some people had begun the day on a cautious note, but with the market showing no signs of weakness during the session, they completed their buy orders. "We were obviously bouncing off quite a strong support level around that 12,800 level," he said.
However the H-share index fell 47.64 points, or 5.08 percent, to 890.35 after China said over the weekend that its domestic stock markets were overheated.
Shanghai's A-share index tumbled 115.370 points, or 9.92 percent, to 1,047.68 and the B-share index dropped 6.362 points, or 9.6 percent, to 59.929.

Analysts said Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting had kept some investors on the sidelines this session, contributing to the lower volume compared with a daily average of HK$9.52 billion last week.

"Most local investors in Hong Kong are staying on the sidelines to get a feeling of what the Dow will do in the next couple of days and the outcome of the FOMC meeting," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.
However, analysts said they expected interest rates to be left unchanged, which Kwong said was encouraging buying.
"If interest rates are unchanged then the market could head higher," he said, adding that the Hang Seng index could test 13,200 points this week before profit-taking sets in.

Shares in Guangdong Tannery, a unit of Guangdong Investment, made a strong trading debut on Monday. The shares more than doubled at the start of trade, opening at HK$2.50 compared with an issue price of HK$1.03. They closed the session at HK$2.05.
Shares in Karrie International did not fare so well. The stock made its trading debut at HK$1.40 compared with an issue price of HK$1.15 and closed at HK$1.02.
